summary:
Plan for w205 (work-queue r34-r39) written up to one open question.
What changes: scripts/work gains `work list` and an optional target for `work show`; a new module scripts/workqueue_list.py (with a CLAUDE.md row); a new step module.
`show` with no target is kept, because requests#r13 still needs it. `work status` is kept, because w205 retires nothing. As a result no existing test breaks.
`show <initiative>` prints what `status <initiative>` prints today (r36 = deprecated r16). Targets are resolved by workqueue.entry or workqueue.find, and refused under r7.
Question: r39 needs `work list` to know which requests an initiative raised into an upstream, and whether each is delivered. Those requests are kept only in the upstream's repository; this context keeps no record of them, and `--raised-for` is not built. How it learns this changes what the narrator sees.
questions: work-queue#r39: how does `work list` in this context know that a request an initiative raised into an upstream is not yet `delivered`? Requests are kept only in the upstream's repository (requests Implementation, decision 0067), and this context keeps no record of one it raised. Reading A: this context keeps its own record of each request it raised (which upstream, the request's id there, the initiative it was raised for, and its last known status). `work list` reads only that record. The narrator sees i1 as waiting on q1 until that record is updated, even after the upstream delivers, and `work list` never fails because the upstream cannot be reached. Reading B: `work list` reads each raised request where it is kept, in the upstream's repository, through a registered location of the upstream. The narrator sees the upstream's current status, so the waiting line goes as soon as the upstream delivers. But `work list` depends on reaching the upstream and exits with an error, or prints the status as unknown, when it cannot. Reading C: a request raised into an upstream is also kept in this context's .shop/work/requests/, with its asker as this context, its upstream named and `part_of`/`source` naming the initiative, as work-queue r23 reads requests. `work list` reads that copy. The narrator sees what reading A gives, and the copy's status follows the upstream only when `work` writes it there.
